title: Sunny Counts the Stars | Bedtime Story
description: Join Sonny the little quokka as she wanders outside on a quiet evening and tries to count every star in the sky. A gentle bedtime story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales, perfect for winding down at the end of the day.
narration:
In a quiet little corner of the Australian bush, when the sky turned the colour of peaches and plums, a sweet little quokka named Sunny was lying in her cosy nest. She blinked her big round eyes and listened. The bush was very still. The kookaburras had gone quiet. The breeze had gone to sleep. But Sunny... Sunny was still awake.

She padded softly outside, her tiny paws brushing the warm red earth. Above her, the sky was enormous and deep and dark, and it was filled — absolutely filled — with stars.

"I'm going to count them," Sunny decided, in her small, cheerful voice. "One... two... three..."

But then she noticed an old possum sitting very still in the fork of a gum tree, his silver fur glowing softly in the moonlight.

"Hello, little one," he said, in a voice as slow and warm as treacle. "What are you doing out on a night like this?"

"I'm counting the stars," said Sunny proudly.

The old possum smiled, gentle and wide. "I have been sitting in this tree for many, many years," he said quietly, "and I have never once been able to count them all. Do you know why?"

Sunny shook her head.

"Because there are too many. And that," he said softly, "is exactly what makes them magical."

Sunny looked up. The stars blinked back, slowly, like tiny friends saying goodnight. She yawned — a long, soft yawn — and curled up right there beneath the open sky, the warm earth beneath her and the whole glittering universe above.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, stars. Goodnight, little one.
